title: Self-taught, exercise books and first reading in Alonzo Ross's band
summary: Hall was largely self-taught with a musical family, bought exercise books, and first read arrangements in Alonzo Ross's band in Florida.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I was wondering, in regard to your, you say you were mostly self-taught I guess, I know your father and all your brothers and all played a lot too, so it's really like having a lot of teachers around everybody you heard. But did you ever have many formal lessons, or actually take up a book to read and all that, if there was any time, when did you?
Yeah, well I bought, I bought some exercise books, you know, and I used to look in them, you know what I mean, get different chords, and all that kind of stuff.
When did you first start using arrangements in bands that you had to do in your reading with the band?
Well, when I left and went to Florida, with Alonzo Ross' band. They had arranger in the band, we used to have rehearsing, get the thing down, you know.
Had you ever read before that? No.
Well I knew, I know, I know what the notes on the client, and after I got the notes, you know, one in the space to get the syncopation, that's all it did.
